To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
porous Si–C–N–O aerogels were prepared by polymer pyrolysis of poly(methylsilsesquioxane).

the polymer-derived ceramics here synthesized can efficiently remove water-soluble organic pollutants, including dyes and other contaminants, from water, with high capacity and selectivity, and can be easily regenerated.

the polymer-derived ceramic aerogel SiOC was found to be an excellent adsorbent for methylene blue and Rhodamine B from aqueous solution, with a maximum adsorption capacity up to 45 mg of methylene blue per gram of SiOC aerogels.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the preparation and characterization of innovative porous nanocomposites for the removal of water-soluble organic dyes, with the aim of finding new materials for the treatment of wastewater from the textile industry and from the environment.
the development of new porous nanocomposites with a free carbon phase dispersed in a silicon carbide–silicon oxycarbides network, which are able to adsorb dyes from water.
a new approach to develop a regenerable, efficient and cost-effective adsorbent for the removal of organic dyes from textile wastewater.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
polymer-derived ceramics of Si–C– O system can be considered as a promising and sustainable alternative for removal of water-soluble pollutants from textile and other industrial wastewaters.
the polymer-derived SiOC aerogels are promising materials for removal of dyes from water.
the SiOC aerogeles are very effective for removing dyes from textile wastewater.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adsorption process is controlled by intra-pore and/or film diffusion and that the adsorption of the two dyes is not influenced by the matrix composition.
polymer-derived ceramics, with a free carbon phase dispersed in an amorphous silicon carbide/sicarbide network, can be used as adsorbents for removal of water-soluble organic dyes.
porous silicon carbide/silanocarbon nanocomposites, prepared by polymer pyrolysis, are promising sorbents for the treatment of colored textile wastewater.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Si–C-O system is a versatile matrix for the preparation of porous, regenerable, and efficient sorbents.
the polymer-derived ceramics of SiOC aerogels are promising adsorbents for the removal of dyes from wastewater.
Si-based polymer-derived nanocomposites can be used to remove dyes from textile and other industrial wastewaters, even when they contain high amounts of metal ions.
